questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an attribute of a population?
questions.solution_text: Natality, Mortality, and Sex ratio are all population attributes. Species interaction is a property of populations interacting with each other, not an attribute of a single population.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The process of growth is maximum during
questions.solution_text: In exponential growth, the initial growth is slow (lag phase) and it increases rapidly thereafter at an exponential rate in log or exponential phase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The roots that originate from the base of the stem are
questions.solution_text: The roots that originate from the base of the stem are fibrous roots.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Match the following diseases with the causative organism and select the correct option.
Column-I: (a) Typhoid (b) Pneumonia (c) Filariasis (d) Malaria
Column-II: (i) Wuchereria (ii) Plasmodium (iii) Salmonella (iv) Haemophilus
questions.solution_text: Typhoid is caused by Salmonella typhi. Pneumonia is caused by Haemophilus influenzae. Filariasis is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti. Malaria is caused by Plasmodium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In which of the following techniques, the embryos are transferred to assist those females who cannot conceive?
questions.solution_text: ZIFT (Zygote Intrafallopian Transfer) and IUT (Intra Uterine Transfer) are embryo transfer methods. GIFT transfers gametes and ICSI injects sperm directly into ovum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Identify the wrong statement with reference to the gene 'I' that controls ABO blood groups.

options.text: A person will have only two of the three alleles.
When IA and IB are present together, they express same type of sugar.
Allele 'i' does not produce any sugar.

questions.solution_text: IA and IB produce slightly different forms of the sugar, not the same type. Allele i does not produce any sugar. Humans can have at most two of the three alleles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Choose the correct pair from the following

options.text: Ligases - Join the two DNA molecules
Polymerases - Break the DNA into fragments
Nucleases - Separate the two strands of DNA
Exonucleases - Make cuts at specific positions within DNA

questions.solution_text: Ligases join two DNA molecules. Polymerases synthesise DNA/RNA. Nucleases cleave DNA. Exonucleases remove nucleotides from ends, while endonucleases cut at internal positions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Select the correct match

options.text: Sickle cell anaemia – Autosomal recessive trait, chromosome-11

questions.solution_text: Sickle cell anaemia is an autosomal recessive trait caused by a mutation in the gene on chromosome 11. Haemophilia is X-linked recessive. Phenylketonuria is autosomal recessive. Thalassemia is autosomal recessive.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column-I: (a) Gregarious, polyphagous pest (b) Adult with radial symmetry and larva with bilateral symmetry (c) Book lungs (d) Bioluminescence
Column-II: (i) Asterias (ii) Scorpion (iii) Ctenoplana (iv) Locusta
questions.solution_text: Locusta is a gregarious pest. Asterias (echinoderm) has radially symmetrical adults and bilaterally symmetrical larvae. Scorpion breathes through book lungs. Ctenoplana (ctenophore) shows bioluminescence.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The infectious stage of Plasmodium that enters the human body is
questions.solution_text: Plasmodium enters the human body as sporozoites (infectious stage) through the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquito.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Identify the substances having glycosidic bond and peptide bond, respectively in their structure
questions.solution_text: Inulin is a polysaccharide of fructose units linked by glycosidic bonds. Insulin is a protein of 51 amino acids linked by peptide bonds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
The plant parts which consist of two generations - one within the other
(a) Pollen grains inside the anther
(b) Germinated pollen grain with two male gametes
(c) Seed inside the fruit
(d) Embryo sac inside the ovule
questions.solution_text: Pollen grain (haploid gametophyte) inside anther (diploid sporophyte) and embryo sac (haploid) inside ovule (diploid) represent two generations one within the other.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The product(s) of reaction catalyzed by nitrogenase in root nodules of leguminous plants is/are
questions.solution_text: N2 + 8e⁻ + 8H⁺ + 16ATP → 2NH3 + H2 + 16ADP + 16Pi. Nitrogenase produces both ammonia and hydrogen gas.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Identify the correct statement with regard to G1 phase (Gap 1) of interphase.

options.text: DNA synthesis or replication takes place.
Reorganisation of all cell components takes place.
Cell is metabolically active, grows but does not replicate its DNA.

questions.solution_text: During G1 phase the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA. DNA synthesis occurs in S phase; nuclear division in M phase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Cuboidal epithelium with brush border of microvilli is found in
questions.solution_text: Cuboidal epithelium with brush border of microvilli is found in the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about inclusion bodies is incorrect?

options.text: They are not bound by any membrane
These are involved in ingestion of food particles
They lie free in the cytoplasm
These represent reserve material in cytoplasm

questions.solution_text: Inclusion bodies are not involved in ingestion of food particles. They are non-living reserves lying free in the cytoplasm, not bound by membranes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids in eukaryotic cells?
questions.solution_text: Golgi bodies are the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids in eukaryotic cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In gel electrophoresis, separated DNA fragments can be visualized with the help of
questions.solution_text: Separated DNA fragments are visualised by staining with Ethidium bromide followed by exposure to UV radiation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Identify the wrong statement with reference to transport of oxygen

options.text: Binding of oxygen with haemoglobin is mainly related to partial pressure of O2
Partial pressure of CO2 can interfere with O2 binding with haemoglobin
Higher H+ conc. in alveoli favours the formation of oxyhaemoglobin
Low pCO2 in alveoli favours the formation of oxyhaemoglobin

questions.solution_text: Higher H+ concentration favours dissociation of oxyhaemoglobin in tissues, not its formation. In alveoli, low pCO2, high pO2, and lesser H+ concentration favour oxyhaemoglobin formation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Ray florets have
questions.solution_text: Ray florets have inferior ovary. They belong to family Asteraceae (e.g. Sunflower) which has epigynous flowers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The specific palindromic sequence which is recognized by EcoRI is
questions.solution_text: EcoRI recognises the palindromic sequence 5'-GAATTC-3' / 3'-CTTAAG-5' and cuts between G and A on both strands.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Identify the wrong statement with regard to Restriction Enzymes.

options.text: Each restriction enzyme functions by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence.
They cut the strand of DNA at palindromic sites.
They are useful in genetic engineering.
Sticky ends can be joined by using DNA ligases.

questions.solution_text: Option 4 is actually correct — DNA ligases do join sticky ends. The wrong statement is Option 1: restriction enzymes function by inspecting specific sequences, not the length of DNA. Note: NCERT states they inspect the length as part of recognising the sequence, so Option 1 is considered the 'wrong' option in the context of this question as per the official answer key (Answer 4 is correct as per PDF — the question asks for the wrong statement and the answer is 4, meaning option 4 is wrong). Actually per the PDF: Answer is 4, implying option 4 is the incorrect statement. But DNA ligases do join sticky ends — this is correct. Re-reading: the PDF states Answer (4) as a correction to option 1 being the wrong statement contextually. Deferring to official answer: sticky ends are joined by ligases which is correct, so option 4 is not wrong. The PDF confirms Answer (4) for this question.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is put into Anaerobic sludge digester for further sewage treatment?
questions.solution_text: Activated sludge (sediment from settlement tank) is pumped into anaerobic sludge digesters. A small part is returned to the aeration tank.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Select the correct events that occur during inspiration.
(a) Contraction of diaphragm
(b) Contraction of external inter-costal muscles
(c) Pulmonary volume decreases
(d) Intra pulmonary pressure increases
questions.solution_text: During inspiration, the diaphragm contracts (increasing thoracic volume in anterio-posterior axis) and external intercostal muscles contract (increasing thoracic volume in dorsoventral axis). Pulmonary volume increases and intrapulmonary pressure decreases.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: If the head of cockroach is removed, it may live for few days because

options.text: the supra-oesophageal ganglia of the cockroach are situated in ventral part of abdomen.
the cockroach does not have nervous system.
the head holds a small proportion of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the ventral part of its body.
the head holds a 1/3rd of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the dorsal part of its body.

questions.solution_text: The head holds only a small proportion of the nervous system; the bulk is distributed along the ventral part of the body, allowing the cockroach to survive briefly after decapitation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are true for the phylum-Chordata?
(a) In Urochordata notochord extends from head to tail and is present throughout their life.
(b) In Vertebrata notochord is present during the embryonic period only.
(c) Central nervous system is dorsal and hollow.
(d) Chordata is divided into 3 subphyla: Hemichordata, Tunicata and Cephalochordata.
questions.solution_text: In Vertebrata, notochord is present only during embryonic period, replaced later by the vertebral column. In chordates, CNS is dorsal and hollow. Statement (a) is wrong as notochord in Urochordata is present only in larval tail. Statement (d) is wrong as Hemichordata is not a subphylum of Chordata.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Match the organism with its use in biotechnology.
(a) Bacillus thuringiensis (b) Thermus aquaticus (c) Agrobacterium tumefaciens (d) Salmonella typhimurium
(i) Cloning vector (ii) Construction of first rDNA molecule (iii) DNA polymerase (iv) Cry proteins
questions.solution_text: Bacillus thuringiensis produces Cry proteins. Thermus aquaticus is the source of Taq polymerase (thermostable DNA polymerase). Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a cloning vector. Salmonella typhimurium was used in constructing the first recombinant DNA molecule.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Match the following concerning essential elements and their functions in plants.
(a) Iron (b) Zinc (c) Boron (d) Manganese
(i) Photolysis of water (ii) Pollen germination (iii) Required for chlorophyll biosynthesis (iv) IAA biosynthesis
questions.solution_text: Iron is essential for chlorophyll biosynthesis. Zinc is needed for synthesis of auxin (IAA). Boron plays a role in pollen germination. Manganese is involved in splitting of water during photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Identify the incorrect statement.

options.text: Heart wood does not conduct water but gives mechanical support
Sapwood is involved in conduction of water and minerals from root to leaf
Sapwood is the innermost secondary xylem and is lighter in colour
Due to deposition of tannins, resins, oils etc., heart wood is dark in colour

questions.solution_text: Sapwood is the outermost secondary xylem (not innermost). It is lighter in colour. Heartwood is the innermost, darker secondary xylem due to deposition of tannins, resins and oils.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Match the following:
(a) Inhibitor of catalytic activity (b) Possess peptide bonds (c) Cell wall material in fungi (d) Secondary metabolite
(i) Ricin (ii) Malonate (iii) Chitin (iv) Collagen
questions.solution_text: Malonate is a competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase. Collagen is a protein with peptide bonds. Chitin is a homopolymer in fungal cell walls. Ricin is a secondary metabolite (toxin).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subtopic: Completion of Meiosis in Secondary Oocyte
questions.question_text: Meiotic division of the secondary oocyte is completed

options.text: At the time of fusion of a sperm with an ovum

questions.solution_text: Meiosis II of secondary oocyte is completed after the entry of sperm, leading to formation of a large ovum and a tiny second polar body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: According to Robert May, the global species diversity is about
questions.solution_text: Robert May estimated global species diversity at about 7 million. Extreme estimates range from 20 to 50 million.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The first phase of translation is
questions.solution_text: The first phase of translation involves activation of amino acids in the presence of ATP and linking them to their cognate tRNA — called charging of tRNA or aminoacylation of tRNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following regions of the globe exhibits highest species diversity?
questions.solution_text: The Amazonian rain forest in South America has the greatest biodiversity on earth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.text: In man insulin is synthesised as a proinsulin
The proinsulin has an extra peptide called C-peptide.
The functional insulin has A and B chains linked together by hydrogen bonds.
Genetically engineered insulin is produced in E. coli.

questions.solution_text: Functional insulin has A and B chains linked by disulphide bridges, not hydrogen bonds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
The transverse section of a plant shows following anatomical features:
(a) Large number of scattered vascular bundles surrounded by bundle sheath
(b) Large conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue
(c) Vascular bundles conjoint and closed
(d) Phloem parenchyma absent
Identify the category of plant and its part:
questions.solution_text: All features — scattered vascular bundles with bundle sheath, large ground tissue, conjoint closed vascular bundles, absence of phloem parenchyma — are characteristic of monocotyledonous stem.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column-I: (a) 6-15 pairs of gill slits (b) Heterocercal caudal fin (c) Air Bladder (d) Poison sting
Column-II: (i) Trygon (ii) Cyclostomes (iii) Chondrichthyes (iv) Osteichthyes
questions.solution_text: Cyclostomes have 6-15 pairs of gill slits. Chondrichthyes have heterocercal caudal fin. Osteichthyes have air bladder for buoyancy. Trygon (cartilaginous fish) has a poison sting.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: From his experiments, S.L. Miller produced amino acids by mixing the following in a closed flask

options.text: CH4, H2, NH3 and water vapor at 800°C
CH3, H2, NH4 and water vapor at 800°C
CH4, H2, NH3 and water vapor at 600°C
CH3, H2, NH3 and water vapor at 600°C

questions.solution_text: In 1953, S.L. Miller created electric discharge in a closed flask containing CH4, H2, NH3 and water vapor at 800°C to produce amino acids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Embryological support for evolution was disapproved by
questions.solution_text: Karl Ernst von Baer disapproved embryological support for evolution, noting that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals during their development.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The process responsible for facilitating loss of water in liquid form from the tip of grass blades at night and in early morning is
questions.solution_text: Root pressure is a positive hydrostatic pressure that develops in tracheary elements at night and early morning, causing guttation (loss of water in liquid form from leaf tips).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Secondary metabolites such as nicotine, strychnine and caffeine are produced by plants for their
questions.solution_text: Nicotine, caffeine, quinine, strychnine and opium are secondary metabolites produced by plants as defences against grazers and browsers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The oxygenation activity of RuBisCO enzyme in photorespiration leads to the formation of

options.text: 1 molecule of 4-C compound and 1 molecule of 2-C compound

questions.solution_text: In photorespiration, O2 binds to RuBisCO instead of CO2. RuBP (5C) is cleaved to form one molecule of phosphoglycerate (3C compound) and one molecule of phosphoglycolate (2C compound). Hence one 3C compound is produced.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Bt cotton variety that was developed by the introduction of toxin gene of Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is resistant to
questions.solution_text: Bt cotton is resistant to cotton bollworm (insect pest). Cry IAc and Cry IIAb genes introduced protect it from cotton bollworm, making it act as a biopesticide.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following refer to correct example(s) of organisms which have evolved due to changes in environment brought about by anthropogenic action?
(a) Darwin's Finches of Galapagos islands.
(b) Herbicide resistant weeds.
(c) Drug resistant eukaryotes.
(d) Man-created breeds of domesticated animals like dogs.
questions.solution_text: Herbicide resistant weeds, drug resistant eukaryotes and man-created dog breeds are examples of anthropogenic evolution. Darwin's Finches are examples of natural selection and adaptive radiation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Identify the wrong statement with reference to immunity.

options.text: When exposed to antigen (living or dead) antibodies are produced in the host's body. It is called 'Active immunity'.
When ready-made antibodies are directly given, it is called 'Passive immunity'.
Active immunity is quick and gives full response.
Foetus receives some antibodies from mother, it is an example for passive immunity.

questions.solution_text: Active immunity is slow and takes time to give its full effective response, in comparison to passive immunity where pre-formed antibodies are administered.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.question_text: By which method was a new breed 'Hisardale' of sheep formed by using Bikaneri ewes and Marino rams?
questions.solution_text: Hisardale is a sheep breed developed in Punjab by cross breeding Bikaneri ewes and Marino rams. Cross breeding involves mating superior males of one breed with superior females of another.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Identify the correct statement with reference to human digestive system.

options.text: Serosa is the innermost layer of the alimentary canal
IIeum is a highly coiled part

questions.solution_text: Ileum is a highly coiled tube. Serosa is the outermost (not innermost) layer. Vermiform appendix arises from caecum. Ileum opens into the large intestine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column-I: (a) Clostridium butylicum (b) Trichoderma polysporum (c) Monascus purpureus (d) Aspergillus niger
Column-II: (i) Cyclosporin-A (ii) Butyric Acid (iii) Citric Acid (iv) Blood cholesterol lowering agent
questions.solution_text: Clostridium butylicum produces butyric acid. Trichoderma polysporum produces Cyclosporin-A (immunosuppressant). Monascus purpureus produces blood cholesterol-lowering statins. Aspergillus niger produces citric acid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Presence of which of the following conditions in urine are indicative of Diabetes Mellitus?
questions.solution_text: Presence of ketone bodies in urine (Ketonuria) and glucose in urine (Glycosuria) are indicative of Diabetes mellitus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Floridean starch has structure similar to
questions.solution_text: Floridean starch is the stored food in red algae. Its structure is similar to amylopectin and glycogen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Select the option including all sexually transmitted diseases.
questions.solution_text: Gonorrhoea (Neisseria gonorrhoeae), Syphilis (Treponema pallidum) and Genital herpes (Herpes simplex virus type II) are all sexually transmitted diseases.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Match the following with respect to meiosis:
(a) Zygotene (b) Pachytene (c) Diplotene (d) Diakinesis
(i) Terminalization (ii) Chiasmata (iii) Crossing over (iv) Synapsis
questions.solution_text: Zygotene: Synapsis. Pachytene: Crossing over. Diplotene: Chiasmata formation. Diakinesis: Terminalization.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs is of unicellular algae?
questions.solution_text: Chlorella and Spirulina are unicellular algae. Laminaria, Sargassum, Gelidium and Gracilaria are multicellular. Volvox is colonial. Anabaena is a cyanobacterium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following hormone levels will cause release of ovum (ovulation) from the Graafian follicle?
questions.solution_text: High estrogen level sends a positive feedback to the anterior pituitary causing LH surge (LH peak). This LH surge leads to ovulation from the Graafian follicle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column-I: (a) Bt cotton (b) Adenosine deaminase deficiency (c) RNAi (d) PCR
Column-II: (i) Gene therapy (ii) Cellular defence (iii) Detection of HIV infection (iv) Bacillus thuringiensis
questions.solution_text: Bt cotton uses toxin gene from Bacillus thuringiensis. ADA deficiency was the first condition treated by gene therapy. RNAi is a mechanism of cellular defence. PCR is used to detect HIV in AIDS patients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Montreal protocol was signed in 1987 for control of

options.text: Transport of Genetically modified organisms from one country to another

questions.solution_text: Montreal Protocol was signed on 16 September 1987 (Ozone Day) and came into force on 1 January 1989. It aimed at stopping production and import of ozone depleting substances (ODS).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about viroids?

options.text: They have RNA with protein coat
They have free RNA without protein coat
They have DNA with protein coat
They have free DNA without protein coat

questions.solution_text: Viroids consist of free RNA (without any protein coat). They are smaller than viruses and cause diseases in plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The ovary is half inferior in:
questions.solution_text: The ovary is half inferior in Plum (perigynous flower). Brinjal and Mustard have superior ovary; Sunflower has inferior ovary.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The enzyme enterokinase helps in conversion of
questions.solution_text: Enterokinase, secreted by intestinal mucosa, activates trypsinogen (from pancreas) into active trypsin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Match the trophic levels with their correct species examples in grassland ecosystem.
(a) Fourth trophic level (b) Second trophic level (c) First trophic level (d) Third trophic level
(i) Crow (ii) Vulture (iii) Rabbit (iv) Grass
questions.solution_text: In grassland: T1=Grass, T2=Rabbit, T3=Crow, T4=Vulture.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: How many true breeding pea plant varieties did Mendel select as pairs, which were similar except in one character with contrasting traits?
questions.solution_text: Mendel selected 14 true breeding plant varieties (7 pairs of contrasting traits).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column-I: (a) Organ of Corti (b) Cochlea (c) Eustachian tube (d) Stapes
Column-II: (i) Connects middle ear and pharynx (ii) Coiled part of the labyrinth (iii) Attached to the oval window (iv) Located on the basilar membrane
questions.solution_text: Organ of Corti is on the basilar membrane. Cochlea is the coiled portion of labyrinth. Eustachian tube connects middle ear to pharynx. Stapes is attached to the oval window.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In water hyacinth and water lily, pollination takes place by:
questions.solution_text: Water hyacinth and water lily produce flowers that emerge above the water level and are pollinated by insects or wind, not by water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name the plant growth regulator which upon spraying on sugarcane crop, increases the length of stem, thus increasing the yield of sugarcane crop.
questions.solution_text: Spraying gibberellins on sugarcane increases stem length, increasing yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In light reaction, plastoquinone facilitates the transfer of electrons from
questions.solution_text: After excitation of PS-II (P680), electrons pass to pheophytin (primary acceptor) then to plastoquinone (PQ), which transfers electrons to the Cytb6f complex.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an inhibitory substance governing seed dormancy?
questions.solution_text: Gibberellic acid breaks seed dormancy by activating synthesis of α-amylase. It is not an inhibitor. ABA, phenolic acids and para-ascorbic acid cause dormancy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name the enzyme that facilitates opening of DNA helix during transcription.
questions.solution_text: RNA polymerase facilitates the opening of DNA helix during transcription.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following would help in prevention of diuresis?

options.text: More water reabsorption due to undersecretion of ADH
Reabsorption of Na+ and water from renal tubules due to aldosterone
Decrease in secretion of renin by JG cells

questions.solution_text: Aldosterone (mineralocorticoid from adrenal cortex) increases reabsorption of Na+ and water from renal tubules, thereby preventing diuresis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In relation to Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity of an ecosystem, which one of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Gross primary productivity is always less than net primary productivity
Gross primary productivity is always more than net primary productivity
Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity are one and same
There is no relationship between Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity

questions.solution_text: NPP = GPP – Respiration. Therefore GPP is always greater than NPP.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column-I: (a) Placenta (b) Zona pellucida (c) Bulbo-urethral glands (d) Leydig cells
Column-II: (i) Androgens (ii) Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) (iii) Layer of the ovum (iv) Lubrication of the Penis
questions.solution_text: Placenta secretes hCG. Zona pellucida is a layer of the ovum. Bulbo-urethral glands secrete fluid for lubrication of penis. Leydig cells secrete androgens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Strobili or cones are found in
questions.solution_text: Strobili or cones are found in Equisetum (horsetails), a pteridophyte.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Some dividing cells exit the cell cycle and enter vegetative inactive stage. This is called quiescent stage (G0). This process occurs at the end of
questions.solution_text: Cells enter the G0 (quiescent) stage at the end of M phase and beginning of G1 phase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Flippers of Penguins and Dolphins are examples of
questions.solution_text: Flippers of penguins and dolphins are analogous organs (similar function, different origin) — a result of convergent evolution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: If the distance between two consecutive base pairs is 0.34 nm and the total number of base pairs of a DNA double helix in a typical mammalian cell is 6.6 × 10⁹ bp, then the length of the DNA is approximately

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The QRS complex in a standard ECG represents
questions.solution_text: QRS complex represents the depolarisation of ventricles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column-I: (a) Eosinophils (b) Basophils (c) Neutrophils (d) Lymphocytes
Column-II: (i) Immune response (ii) Phagocytosis (iii) Release histaminase, destructive enzymes (iv) Release granules containing histamine
questions.solution_text: Eosinophils release histaminase and destructive enzymes (allergic reactions). Basophils secrete histamine. Neutrophils are phagocytic. Lymphocytes are responsible for immune responses.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Adenine pairs with thymine through two H-bonds
Adenine pairs with thymine through one H-bond
Adenine pairs with thymine through three H-bonds
Adenine does not pair with thymine

questions.solution_text: Adenine pairs with thymine through two hydrogen bonds (A=T). Guanine pairs with cytosine through three hydrogen bonds (G≡C).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The sequence that controls the copy number of the linked DNA in the vector, is termed
questions.solution_text: The Ori (origin of replication) sequence controls copy number of linked DNA in the vector and initiates replication.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Identify the basic amino acid from the following.
questions.solution_text: Lysine is a basic amino acid. Valine is neutral, Glutamic acid is acidic, and Tyrosine is aromatic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column-I: (a) Pituitary gland (b) Thyroid gland (c) Adrenal gland (d) Pancreas
Column-II: (i) Grave's disease (ii) Diabetes mellitus (iii) Diabetes insipidus (iv) Addison's disease
questions.solution_text: Diabetes insipidus: hyporelease of ADH from posterior pituitary. Grave's disease: excess thyroid hormones. Addison's disease: hyposecretion of adrenal cortex. Diabetes mellitus: hyposecretion of insulin from pancreatic β-cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Select the correct statement.

options.text: Insulin acts on pancreatic cells and adipocytes.

questions.solution_text: Glucocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, increasing blood sugar. Glucagon is associated with hyperglycemia (raises blood sugar). Insulin acts on hepatocytes and adipocytes and is associated with hypoglycemia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the most abundant protein in the animals?
questions.solution_text: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world. RuBisCO is the most abundant protein in the entire biosphere.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Experimental verification of the chromosomal theory of inheritance was done by
questions.solution_text: Sutton and Boveri proposed the chromosomal theory of inheritance, but it was experimentally verified by T.H. Morgan.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subtopic: Bones of the Thorax and Shoulder
questions.question_text:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column-I: (a) Floating Ribs (b) Acromion (c) Scapula (d) Glenoid cavity
Column-II: (i) Located between second and seventh ribs (ii) Head of the Humerus (iii) Clavicle (iv) Do not connect with the sternum
questions.solution_text: Floating ribs (11th, 12th) do not connect ventrally with sternum. Acromion process of scapula articulates with clavicle. Scapula lies between 2nd and 7th rib. Glenoid cavity articulates with head of humerus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The number of substrate level phosphorylations in one turn of citric acid cycle is
questions.solution_text: There is one substrate-level phosphorylation per turn of the citric acid cycle: Succinyl-CoA → Succinate (via thiokinase), producing GTP which is converted to ATP.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex occurs during
questions.solution_text: The synaptonemal complex dissolves during the Diplotene stage of Prophase I of Meiosis I.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Bilaterally symmetrical and acoelomate animals are exemplified by
questions.solution_text: Platyhelminthes are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and acoelomate animals with organ level of organisation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The body of the ovule is fused within the funicle at
questions.solution_text: The attachment point of the funicle and the body of the ovule is known as the hilum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Goblet cells of alimentary canal are modified from
questions.solution_text: Goblet cells are modified columnar epithelial cells that secrete mucus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Snow-blindness in Antarctic region is due to

options.text: Freezing of fluids in the eye by low temperature
Inflammation of cornea due to high dose of UV-B radiation
High reflection of light from snow
Damage to retina caused by infra-red rays

questions.solution_text: UV-B radiation is absorbed by the cornea; a high dose causes inflammation of the cornea called snow blindness or photokeratitis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Bond Order and Existence of Molecules
questions.question_text: Identify a molecule which does not exist.
questions.solution_text: For He2: electronic configuration is σ1s², σ*1s². Bond order = (2−2)/2 = 0. Since bond order is zero, He2 does not exist.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Find out the solubility of Ni(OH)2 in 0.1 M NaOH. Given that the ionic product of Ni(OH)2 is 2 × 10⁻¹⁵
questions.solution_text: Ksp = [Ni²⁺][OH⁻]². In 0.1M NaOH, [OH⁻] ≈ 0.1M. So 2×10⁻¹⁵ = s × (0.1)². s = 2×10⁻¹³ M.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Identify the correct statements from the following:
(a) CO2(g) is used as refrigerant for ice-cream and frozen food.
(b) The structure of C60 contains twelve six-carbon rings and twenty five-carbon rings.
(c) ZSM-5, a type of zeolite, is used to convert alcohols into gasoline.
(d) CO is colorless and odourless gas.
questions.solution_text: Dry ice is CO2(s) not CO2(g). C60 contains 20 six-membered rings and 12 five-membered rings. ZSM-5 converts alcohols to gasoline (correct). CO is colourless and odourless (correct).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Hydrolysis of sucrose: Sucrose + H₂O → Glucose + Fructose. If Kc = 2 × 10¹³ at 300 K, the value of ΔrG° at the same temperature will be:
questions.solution_text: ΔrG° = −RT ln Keq = −8.314 × 300 × ln(2 × 10¹³)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Identify compound X in the following sequence of reactions: CH3 → (Cl2/hν) → X → (H2O, 373K) → CHO
questions.solution_text: CH3 reacts with Cl2/hν to give CHCl2 (gem-dichloride). CHCl2 on hydrolysis with H2O at 373K gives geminal diol which loses water to form CHO (aldehyde).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Identify the incorrect match.
Name vs IUPAC Official Name:
(a) Unnilunium – Mendelevium
(b) Unniltrium – Lawrencium
(c) Unnilhexium – Seaborgium
(d) Unununium – Darmstadtium
questions.solution_text: Unununium has atomic number 111 and its IUPAC official name is Roentgenium, not Darmstadtium (which is element 110).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An element has a body centered cubic (bcc) structure with a cell edge of 288 pm. The atomic radius is
questions.solution_text: For BCC: 4r = √3a, so r = (√3/4) × 288 pm.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following set of molecules will have zero dipole moment?

options.text: Boron trifluoride, hydrogen fluoride, carbon dioxide, 1,3-dichlorobenzene
Boron trifluoride, beryllium difluoride, carbon dioxide, 1,4-dichlorobenzene

questions.solution_text: BF3 (trigonal planar), BeF2 (linear), CO2 (linear), and 1,4-dichlorobenzene (para, symmetric) all have zero dipole moment due to symmetrical cancellation of bond dipoles.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: On electrolysis of dil. sulphuric acid using Platinum (Pt) electrode, the product obtained at anode will be
questions.solution_text: At anode: 2H2O → O2(g) + 4H⁺(aq) + 4e⁻. At cathode: 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ → 2H2(g).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Reaction between acetone and methylmagnesium chloride followed by hydrolysis will give:
questions.solution_text: Acetone (CH3COCH3) + CH3MgCl → after hydrolysis → (CH3)3COH = tert-butyl alcohol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following oxoacid of sulphur has –O–O– linkage?
questions.solution_text: H2S2O8 (peroxodisulphuric acid) contains the –O–O– (peroxide) linkage between the two sulphur centres.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following amine will give the carbylamine test?
questions.solution_text: Carbylamine (isocyanide) test is positive for primary amines (both aliphatic and aromatic). Aniline is a primary aromatic amine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The calculated spin only magnetic moment of Cr²⁺ ion is
questions.solution_text: Cr: [Ar]3d⁵4s¹. Cr²⁺: [Ar]3d⁴ — 4 unpaired electrons. μ = √(n(n+2)) = √(4×6) = √24 ≈ 4.90 BM.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The correct option for free expansion of an ideal gas under adiabatic condition is
questions.solution_text: Free expansion: Pex = 0, so w = 0. Adiabatic: q = 0. By first law: ΔU = q + w = 0. For ideal gas, ΔU = 0 implies ΔT = 0.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The freezing point depression constant (Kf) of benzene is 5.12 K kg mol⁻¹. The freezing point depression for the solution of molality 0.078 m containing a non-electrolyte solute in benzene is (rounded off upto two decimal places):

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The number of Faradays (F) required to produce 20 g of calcium from molten CaCl2 (Atomic mass of Ca = 40 g mol⁻¹) is
questions.solution_text: Equivalent mass of Ca = 40/2 = 20. Number of equivalents = 20/20 = 1. Therefore 1 Faraday is required.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Reaction between benzaldehyde and acetophenone in presence of dilute NaOH is known as
questions.solution_text: When two different carbonyl compounds (benzaldehyde and acetophenone) react in the presence of dilute NaOH, it is called Cross Aldol condensation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.question_text: Paper chromatography is an example of
questions.solution_text: Paper chromatography is a type of partition chromatography in which chromatography paper serves as the stationary phase.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An increase in the concentration of the reactants of a reaction leads to change in
questions.solution_text: Increasing concentration increases collision frequency, thus increasing reaction rate. Heat of reaction is also an extensive property and changes with concentration/amount, but the primary kinetic effect is collision frequency.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A mixture of N2 and Ar gases in a cylinder contains 7 g of N2 and 8 g of Ar. If the total pressure is 27 bar, the partial pressure of N2 is: [N = 14, Ar = 40]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.ncert_chapter_name: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.question_text: Identify the correct statement from the following:

options.text: Wrought iron is impure iron with 4% carbon.
Blister copper has blistered appearance due to evolution of CO2.
Vapour phase refining is carried out for Nickel by Van Arkel method.
Pig iron can be moulded into a variety of shapes.

questions.solution_text: Pig iron (from blast furnace, ~4% carbon) is cast into a variety of shapes. Wrought iron is the purest form of iron. Van Arkel method is for Ti and Zr, not Ni. Blister copper gets its blistered appearance from SO2, not CO2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A tertiary butyl carbocation is more stable than a secondary butyl carbocation because of?
questions.solution_text: Tertiary butyl carbocation has 9 α-H atoms vs 5 in secondary. More α-H atoms → greater hyperconjugation → greater stability.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a cationic detergent?
questions.solution_text: Cetyltrimethylammonium bromide is a cationic detergent (quaternary ammonium salt). The others are anionic detergents/soaps.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Elimination reaction of 2-Bromo-pentane to form pent-2-ene is
(a) β-Elimination reaction
(b) Follows Zaitsev rule
(c) Dehydrohalogenation reaction
(d) Dehydration reaction
questions.solution_text: Removing H and Br from adjacent carbons makes it β-elimination and dehydrohalogenation. The more substituted alkene (pent-2-ene) is formed, following Zaitsev's rule. Dehydration involves –OH not –Br.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The mixture which shows positive deviation from Raoult's law is
questions.solution_text: Ethanol + Acetone shows positive deviation. Acetone breaks hydrogen bonds between ethanol molecules, weakening intermolecular attractions, so vapour pressure exceeds ideal values.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following is the correct order of increasing field strength of ligands to form coordination compounds?
questions.solution_text: As per the spectrochemical series: SCN⁻ < F⁻ < C2O4²⁻ < CN⁻ in terms of increasing field strength.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a basic amino acid?
questions.solution_text: Lysine is a basic amino acid due to the additional –NH2 group in its side chain.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: HCl was passed through a solution of CaCl2, MgCl2 and NaCl. Which compound(s) crystallise(s)?
questions.solution_text: CaCl2 and MgCl2 are more soluble than NaCl. On passing HCl(g), the common ion (Cl⁻) effect reduces NaCl solubility, causing only NaCl to crystallise out.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a natural polymer?
questions.solution_text: Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene. The others are synthetic polymers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct about carbon monoxide?

options.text: It reduces oxygen carrying ability of blood.
The carboxyhaemoglobin (haemoglobin bound to CO) is less stable than oxyhaemoglobin.
It is produced due to incomplete combustion.

questions.solution_text: Carboxyhaemoglobin is about 300 times more stable than oxyhaemoglobin, not less stable.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Sucrose on hydrolysis gives
questions.solution_text: Sucrose on hydrolysis gives α-D-glucose and β-D-fructose.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The following metal ion activates many enzymes, participates in the oxidation of glucose to produce ATP and with Na, is responsible for the transmission of nerve signals.
questions.solution_text: Potassium (K) activates many enzymes, participates in oxidation of glucose to produce ATP, and along with Na is responsible for nerve signal transmission.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which one of the followings has maximum number of atoms?
(1) 1 g of Ag(s) [At. mass 108]
(2) 1 g of Mg(s) [At. mass 24]
(3) 1 g of O2(g) [At. mass O=16]
(4) 1 g of Li(s) [At. mass 7]
questions.solution_text: Atoms in 1g Li = NA/7 (largest, since Li has lowest atomic mass). Ag: NA/108, Mg: NA/24, O atoms: NA/16.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The number of protons, neutrons and electrons in ¹⁷⁵₇₁Lu, respectively, are
questions.solution_text: Protons = atomic number = 71. Electrons = 71 (neutral atom). Neutrons = mass number − protons = 175 − 71 = 104.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: What is the change in oxidation number of carbon in the following reaction? CH4(g) + 4Cl2(g) → CCl4(l) + 4HCl(g)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Identify the incorrect statement.

options.text: Cr²⁺ (d⁴) is a stronger reducing agent than Fe²⁺ (d⁶) in water.
The transition metals and their compounds are known for their catalytic activity due to their ability to adopt multiple oxidation states and to form complexes.
Interstitial compounds are those that are formed when small atoms like H, C or N are trapped inside the crystal lattices of metals.
The oxidation states of chromium in CrO4²⁻ and Cr2O7²⁻ are not the same.

questions.solution_text: Chromium is in +6 oxidation state in both CrO4²⁻ and Cr2O7²⁻. The statement that they are not the same is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For the reaction, 2Cl(g) → Cl2(g), the correct option is:
questions.solution_text: Cl2(g) → 2Cl(g) is endothermic (bond breaking), so the reverse reaction 2Cl(g) → Cl2(g) is exothermic: ΔrH < 0. Two gaseous atoms combining into one molecule reduces randomness: ΔrS < 0.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Measuring Zeta potential is useful in determining which property of colloidal solution?
questions.solution_text: Zeta potential is the potential difference between the fixed layer and the diffused layer of opposite charge on colloidal particles. Equal and similar charges on colloidal particles are largely responsible for the stability of the colloidal solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Urea reacts with water to form A which will decompose to form B. B when passed through Cu²⁺(aq), deep blue colour solution C is formed. What is the formula of C from the following?
questions.solution_text: NH2CONH2 + H2O → (NH4)2CO3 (A) → NH3 (B) + CO2 + H2O. NH3 passed through Cu²⁺(aq) forms [Cu(NH3)4]²⁺ (C), a deep blue coloured complex (Schweizer's reagent).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the following and identify the correct option.
(a) CO(g) + H2(g)
(b) Temporary hardness of water
(c) B2H6
(d) H2O2
(i) Mg(HCO3)2 + Ca(HCO3)2
(ii) An electron deficient hydride
(iii) Synthesis gas
(iv) Non-planar structure
questions.solution_text: CO + H2 mixture is synthesis gas (water gas). Temporary hardness is due to bicarbonates of Ca and Mg. B2H6 (diborane) is an electron deficient hydride. H2O2 has a non-planar open book structure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question_text:
Match the following:
Oxide → Nature
(a) CO → (i) Basic
(b) BaO → (ii) Neutral
(c) Al2O3 → (iii) Acidic
(d) Cl2O7 → (iv) Amphoteric
questions.solution_text: CO is a neutral oxide. BaO is a basic oxide. Al2O3 is an amphoteric oxide. Cl2O7 is an acidic oxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The rate constant for a first order reaction is 4.606 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. The time required to reduce 2.0 g of the reactant to 0.2 g is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An alkene on ozonolysis gives methanal as one of the products. Its structure is
questions.solution_text: CH2=CH–CH2–CH3 on ozonolysis gives methanal (HCHO) from the =CH2 end and propanal (CH3CH2CHO) from the other carbon. Methanal is only produced when one carbon of the double bond bears two H atoms (=CH2 group).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following alkane cannot be made in good yield by Wurtz reaction?
questions.solution_text: Wurtz reaction gives good yield only with symmetrical alkanes (same alkyl halide on both sides). n-Heptane has an odd number of carbons and cannot be made from a single type of alkyl halide; it would require two different halides, giving a mixture of three alkanes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Anisole on cleavage with HI gives
questions.solution_text: Anisole (C6H5–O–CH3) on reaction with HI undergoes SN2 attack on the methyl group (weaker C–O bond), giving phenol (C6H5OH) and methyl iodide (CH3I). The aryl–oxygen bond is not cleaved under normal conditions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For which one of the following, Bohr model is not valid?
questions.solution_text: Bohr model is valid only for single-electron species (hydrogen-like atoms). Singly ionised neon (Ne⁺) has 9 electrons, so the Bohr model is not valid for it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The ratio of contributions made by the electric field and magnetic field components to the intensity of an electromagnetic wave is: (c = speed of electromagnetic waves)
questions.solution_text: In an electromagnetic wave, the energy is equally shared between the electric and magnetic field components. Hence the ratio of their contributions to intensity is 1:1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The Brewster's angle ib for an interface should be
questions.solution_text: μ = tan(ib). For any real medium μ > 1, so tan(ib) > 1, which means ib > 45°. Also ib < 90°. Hence 45° < ib < 90°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A cylinder contains hydrogen gas at pressure of 249 kPa and temperature 27°C. Its density is: (R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A ray is incident at an angle of incidence i on one surface of a small angle prism (with angle of prism A) and emerges normally from the opposite surface. If the refractive index of the material of the prism is μ, then the angle of incidence is nearly equal to:
questions.solution_text: Emerges normally ⟹ r2 = 0 ⟹ r1 = A. Applying Snell's law: sin i = μ sin A. For small angles: i ≈ μA.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two cylinders A and B of equal capacity are connected to each other via a stop cock. A contains an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure. B is completely evacuated. The entire system is thermally insulated. The stop cock is suddenly opened. The process is:
questions.solution_text: The entire system is thermally insulated, so no heat exchange takes place: q = 0. This makes the process adiabatic. (It is also a free expansion since the gas expands against vacuum.)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The energy equivalent of 0.5 g of a substance is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A body weighs 72 N on the surface of the earth. What is the gravitational force on it, at a height equal to half the radius of the earth?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The solids which have the negative temperature coefficient of resistance are:
questions.solution_text: Metals have a positive temperature coefficient of resistance (resistance increases with temperature). Insulators and semiconductors have a negative temperature coefficient (resistance decreases with temperature).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Phase Difference Between Displacement and Acceleration
questions.question_text: The phase difference between displacement and acceleration of a particle in a simple harmonic motion is:
questions.solution_text: In SHM, y = A sin(ωt) and a = −Aω² sin(ωt) = Aω² sin(ωt + π). The phase difference between displacement and acceleration is π rad.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A screw gauge has least count of 0.01 mm and there are 50 divisions in its circular scale. The pitch of the screw gauge is:
questions.solution_text: Least count = Pitch / Number of divisions on circular scale. Pitch = LC × N = 0.01 mm × 50 = 0.5 mm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a guitar, two strings A and B made of same material are slightly out of tune and produce beats of frequency 6 Hz. When tension in B is slightly decreased, the beat frequency increases to 7 Hz. If the frequency of A is 530 Hz, the original frequency of B will be:
questions.solution_text: Beat frequency = |fA − fB| = 6 Hz. When tension in B decreases, fB decreases and beats increase to 7 Hz. This means fA > fB originally. So fB = fA − 6 = 530 − 6 = 524 Hz.

questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.subtopic: Centre of Mass of Two Particle System
questions.ncert_chapter_name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.ncert_chapter_name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question_text: Find the torque about the origin when a force of 3ĵ N acts on a particle whose position vector is 2k̂ m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Light with an average flux of 20 W/cm² falls on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence having surface area 20 cm². The energy received by the surface during time span of 1 minute is:
questions.solution_text: Energy = Intensity × Area × Time = 20 × 20 × 60 = 24000 J = 24 × 10³ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Electric Field Due to Spherical Conductor
questions.question_text: A spherical conductor of radius 10 cm has a charge of 3.2 × 10⁻⁷ C distributed uniformly. What is the magnitude of electric field at a point 15 cm from the centre of the sphere? (1/4πε₀ = 9×10⁹ N m² C⁻²)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a certain region of space with volume 0.2 m³, the electric potential is found to be 5 V throughout. The magnitude of electric field in this region is:
questions.solution_text: E = −dV/dr. Since V is constant throughout the region, dV/dr = 0, so E = 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The increase in the width of the depletion region in a p-n junction diode is due to:

options.text: Both forward bias and reverse bias

questions.solution_text: Reverse biasing increases the width of the depletion region. Forward biasing decreases it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A 40 μF capacitor is connected to a 200 V, 50 Hz ac supply. The rms value of the current in the circuit is, nearly:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The mean free path for a gas, with molecular diameter d and number density n can be expressed as:
questions.solution_text: The mean free path λ = 1/(√2 × n × πd²), where n is number density and d is molecular diameter.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For transistor action, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Base, emitter and collector regions should have same doping concentrations.
Base, emitter and collector regions should have same size.
Both emitter junction as well as the collector junction are forward biased.
The base region must be very thin and lightly doped.

questions.solution_text: For transistor action: the base must be very thin and lightly doped; emitter is heavily doped; collector is moderately doped. The emitter-base junction is forward biased and collector-base junction is reverse biased.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question_text: Light of frequency 1.5 times the threshold frequency is incident on a photosensitive material. What will be the photoelectric current if the frequency is halved and intensity is doubled?
questions.solution_text: Initial frequency ν = 1.5ν₀. New frequency ν' = ν/2 = 0.75ν₀ < ν₀ (threshold). Since the new frequency is below the threshold, no photoelectric emission occurs. Current = zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: When a uranium isotope ²³⁵₉₂U is bombarded with a neutron, it generates ⁸⁹₃₆Kr, three neutrons and:
questions.solution_text: Conservation of atomic number: 92 + 0 = 36 + Z → Z = 56 (Ba). Conservation of mass number: 235 + 1 = 89 + 3 + A → A = 144. The product is ¹⁴⁴₅₆Ba.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question_text: The energy required to break one bond in DNA is 10⁻²⁰ J. This value in eV is nearly:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two bodies of mass 4 kg and 6 kg are tied to the ends of a massless string. The string passes over a frictionless pulley. The acceleration of the system in terms of acceleration due to gravity (g) is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A wire of length L, area of cross section A is hanging from a fixed support. The length of the wire changes to L1 when mass M is suspended from its free end. The expression for Young's modulus is:
questions.solution_text: Stress = Mg/A; Strain = (L1 − L)/L; Y = Stress/Strain = MgL / [A(L1 − L)].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The average thermal energy for a mono-atomic gas is: (kB is Boltzmann constant and T, absolute temperature)
questions.solution_text: A monoatomic gas has 3 translational degrees of freedom. By equipartition theorem, average energy = (f/2)kBT = (3/2)kBT.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which of the following graph represents the variation of resistivity (ρ) with temperature (T) for copper?

options.text: Nearly linear increase with a deviation at low T

questions.solution_text: For copper (a metal), resistivity increases nearly linearly with temperature at moderate and high temperatures, but deviates considerably from a straight line at very low temperatures (low T region curves away from linearity).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The color code of a resistance is given as Yellow, Violet, Brown, Gold. The values of resistance and tolerance, respectively, are
questions.solution_text: Yellow = 4, Violet = 7, Brown = ×10¹ multiplier, Gold = ±5%. R = 47 × 10 = 470 Ω ± 5%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In Young's double slit experiment, if the separation between coherent sources is halved and the distance of the screen from the coherent sources is doubled, then the fringe width becomes:
questions.solution_text: β = λD/d. New β' = λ(2D)/(d/2) = 4λD/d = 4β. The fringe width becomes four times.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with air as medium is 6 μF. With the introduction of a dielectric medium, the capacitance becomes 30 μF. The permittivity of the medium is: (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C² N⁻¹ m⁻²)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Dimensions of stress are:
questions.solution_text: Stress = Force/Area = [MLT⁻²]/[L²] = [ML⁻¹T⁻²].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Assume that light of wavelength 600 nm is coming from a star. The limit of resolution of telescope whose objective has a diameter of 2 m is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit is connected to an ac voltage source. When L is removed from the circuit, the phase difference between current and voltage is π/3. If instead C is removed from the circuit, the phase difference is again π/3 between current and voltage. The power factor of the circuit is:
questions.solution_text: Without L: tan(π/3) = XC/R. Without C: tan(π/3) = XL/R. So XL = XC — the circuit is at resonance. At resonance Z = R, power factor = cos φ = R/Z = 1.

questions.solution_text: Mobility μ = vd/E = (7.5×10⁻⁴) / (3×10⁻¹⁰) = 2.5×10⁶ m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.

questions.question_text: The quantities of heat required to raise the temperature of two solid copper spheres of radii r1 and r2 (r1 = 1.5 r2) through 1 K are in the ratio:
questions.solution_text: Q = msΔT; m ∝ r³ (for same material and density). Q1/Q2 = (r1/r2)³ = (1.5)³ = 3.375 = 27/8.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Taking into account of the significant figures, what is the value of 9.99 m − 0.0099 m?
questions.solution_text: 9.99 − 0.0099 = 9.9801 m. In subtraction, the result should have the same number of decimal places as the number with the least decimal places (9.99 has 2). So answer = 9.98 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Capillary Rise and Mass of Liquid
questions.question_text: A capillary tube of radius r is immersed in water and water rises in it to a height h. The mass of the water in the capillary is 5 g. Another capillary tube of radius 2r is immersed in water. The mass of water that will rise in this tube is:
questions.solution_text: Surface tension force = 2πrT cosθ = mg. So m ∝ r (since h = 2T cosθ/ρrg, and m = ρπr²h ∝ r). For radius 2r, mass = 2 × 5 = 10 g.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A resistance wire connected in the left gap of a metre bridge balances a 10 Ω resistance in the right gap at a point which divides the bridge wire in the ratio 3:2. If the length of the resistance wire is 1.5 m, then the length of 1 Ω of the resistance wire is:
questions.solution_text: P/10 = 3/2 → P = 15 Ω. Resistance ∝ length. For 1 Ω: length = 1.5/15 = 0.1 m = 1.0×10⁻¹ m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For a logic circuit where inputs A and B each pass through a NOT gate, and the outputs Ā and B̄ are fed into a NOR gate to produce Y, the truth table is:
questions.solution_text: Y = NOR(Ā, B̄) = Ā + B̄ with overbar = NOT(Ā + B̄) = A·B (by De Morgan's theorem). This is an AND gate truth table: Y=1 only when both A=1 and B=1.
